column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health
`/app/run.json` installs, builds and serves the app on port 4173, and `GET /api/health` answers 200 with `{"status": "ok"}` in every grading instance, as qualified in Deployment.

Grading setup route
`POST /api/grading/setup` with the grading key builds the people, workspace, projects, items, links, assignments and baseline it is given and returns their ids, as specified in API.

Sign-in and sign-up
People create an account at `/signup`, sign in at `/signin` or through `POST /api/session`, and every page and API call other than the public ones requires a session.

Server-owned today and late flag
Today comes from the server's configuration, served by `GET /api/config`, and the today line and every late flag follow it whatever the browser's clock says.

Request limits and error order
Every API error follows the one published precedence and body shape, with the body-size and content-type limits from Server boundary.

Working-day calendar
Starts, ends and durations count only the project's working days, a start on a non-working day moves to the next working day, and every screen date uses the published format.

Project read model
`GET /api/projects/<id>` returns the server's one computed schedule with exactly the published keys, and every view and export shows those same values.

Empty project
A project with no items shows the published empty sentence, the `No finish date yet` finish text and an `Open the list` button instead of the chart.

Task list grid
The `Task list` grid has the published columns, one active cell moved by Arrow, Home and End keys, and opens, saves, cancels and adds rows by keyboard as described in Interactions.

Predecessors cell
The Predecessors cell accepts the published entry syntax, shows links in canonical text, replaces the item's incoming links on save, and refuses bad entries with the first published message.

Keyboard reorder and grouping
Alt with the Arrow keys moves a task or milestone up or down a row and into or out of a group, persisted on the server and announced with the published sentences.

Build a plan from the list
The owner builds a linked, grouped plan in an empty project by keyboard alone, and an editor's open chart shows the rows as they are added.

Pointer drag, snap and resize
Dragging a bar's middle moves it and dragging its end handles resizes it, snapping to whole days and then to working days by the published rules, with the drag tip and Escape cancel.

Holidays
Adding or removing a holiday in the Holidays dialog recalculates every item's dates on the server, marks the day in the chart header and announces how many tasks moved.

Re-plan by pointer
The owner drags and resizes bars across a weekend and a holiday and adds a holiday by keyboard, and every resulting date survives a reload.

Bar keyboard
A focused bar moves one working day with ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, changes duration with Shift and the Arrow keys, opens Task details with Enter and the link dialog with L, and keeps focus after every redraw.

Chosen start and link bounds
Each item keeps its chosen start, its shown start is the latest of that and every link bound, and a move earlier than the bound saves the chosen start and announces the published constraint sentence.

Bar descriptions
Every bar's accessible name is the item name and its description is the published sentence of dates, duration, progress, critical, late, variance and links.

Schedule updates announcements
The `Schedule updates` live region announces the published sentence for each of the person's own accepted edits only after the server has answered.

Viewers cannot edit
A viewer can read and export every view but the server refuses every change from them with 403, and the screen tells them so without changing anything.

Re-plan by keyboard
The owner nudges and resizes bars by keyboard and hears each result, while a viewer in another browser cannot change the plan.

Four link types with lag
Finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish and start-to-finish links with a lag from -30 to 30 working days give the published dates.

Link dialog
The `Add link` dialog, opened with L on a focused bar, creates a link by keyboard and returns focus to the bar.

Link errors and loops
Duplicate, self, group, bad-lag and looping links are refused with the published status, body and message, the loop message names the loop path, and nothing is saved.

Link a plan by keyboard
The owner links every item of the Link examples project through the link dialog by keyboard and sees each successor land on its published dates.

Task details dialog
The `Task details` dialog edits an item's name, chosen start, duration and percent, manages assignees and comments, keeps Tab inside itself and returns focus to its opener.

Live updates in place
Every accepted change appears in every other open view of the project without a reload, keeping each viewer's focus and scroll, and is announced in `Project updates`.

Push later, come back earlier
Moving a predecessor later pushes its dependents in the owner's and an editor's open chart, and moving it back lets them return no earlier than their chosen starts.

Critical path and float
The server computes total float and the critical path per accepted edit, marks critical bars, links and the critical count, and the highlight toggle dims every non-critical bar.

Watch the critical path change
The owner moves tasks and sees exactly which items join the critical path in the chart, the list and the API, while an editor's chart shows the same.

Baseline save and replace
Saving a baseline stores every item's shown dates and the finish under a name, and saving again asks for confirmation with the published sentence before replacing it.

Variance and baseline ghosts
Each item and the finish show the signed working-day variance from the baseline in the chart, grid, description and header, and Show baseline draws ghost bars at the baseline dates.

Compare against the baseline
The owner saves a baseline by keyboard, moves a task, and reads every variance, the finish variance and the ghost bars, which survive a reload.

Percent complete and group rollup
Percent complete is a whole number, milestones are 0 or 100, and each group shows the duration-weighted mean of its tasks rounded half up, or 0 when it has no tasks, everywhere it appears.

Phone timeline
Below 768 pixels wide the Gantt view is the `Timeline` card list with short dates, progress, Critical and Late words and an Update progress button per task.

Progress sheet
The `Update progress` sheet sets percent complete with a slider that works by touch, pointer and keyboard in steps of 5 without scrolling the page.

Published breakpoints
The project page shows the published phone, tablet and desktop layout at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 and never scrolls sideways.

Update progress on a phone
An editor on a phone updates a task's progress by touch, sees the card and its group rollup change, and a desktop browser sees the new percent live.

Workload hours
Each person's hours per weekday sum their assignments across every project in the workspace on that project's working days, and a day above capacity is over-allocated.

Workload grid
The `Workload` grid shows two weeks of weekday cells per owner and editor with the published labels and attributes, moves by keyboard and opens each day's breakdown.

Assignments
Owners and editors assign owners and editors to tasks at a number of hours a day and remove them, with the published limits.

Rebalance a person's load
An editor assigns a person to an overlapping task and the owner's open workload grid shows the over-allocated days without a reload.

Version conflicts
An edit based on an older item version is refused with 409 naming who changed it, the sender's screen returns to the server's state with the published notice, and of two simultaneous edits exactly one wins.

Presence and selection
`People here` lists everyone with the project open, and the bar another person has focused carries their name.

Open dialog keeps its edits
An open Task details dialog keeps its unsaved values, focus and version while pushed changes redraw the chart behind it, and takes the current values after a refused save.

Two editors on one task
Two editors edit the same task at once, one change wins, the other sees the conflict notice and saves again successfully.

Comments
Owners and editors post comments on an item, shown oldest first and pushed live to every open Task details dialog for that item, with the 1000-character limit.

Assignment notice
Assigning someone other than yourself sends them one email after the server's configured delay, with the published subject, body and link, and an assignment removed within the delay sends nothing.

Assign and discuss
The owner comments and assigns an editor by keyboard, the editor sees the comment live, receives the notice by email and opens the task from its link.

Export menu and stored files
The Export menu renders a CSV or PDF on the server, stores it in MinIO, and shows its download link only after the stored object is confirmed, listed again after a reload.

CSV content
The CSV export has the published header, one row per item with the server's values and neutralises cells starting with =, +, - or @.

PDF content
The PDF export is A4 landscape with the project name as its title, 20 rows a page, page numbers and each row's published line of text.

Storage outage
While file storage is unreachable an export answers 503, shows the published alert and no link, and health still answers 200.

Export a plan
The owner and a viewer export a plan to CSV and PDF by keyboard and download the stored files.

Knock-on motion
After an accepted edit's result arrives, moved bars slide one dependency depth at a time and the finish marker follows, with the published timings and attributes.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion every bar and the finish marker take their final place in one frame with no motion attributes, and every announcement and shifted mark is unchanged.

Focus and accessibility
Focus is always visible, every dialog and sheet keeps Tab inside itself and closes with Escape, and the Gantt, List and Workload views have no automated accessibility violations at the three published sizes.

Visual language
Every screen uses STIX Two Text, the two inks on off-white, fill, outline and hatch instead of status colours, and yellow on exactly one element, as described in Visual design.

Landing page
The signed-out home page shows the published column-on-one-line hero with its headline, links and true-size demo plan.

Secrets and served assets
Every service credential and URL is read from the environment, none reaches the browser, and the font, icons and code are served by the app itself.
`/app/run.json` exists with the string fields `install`, `build` and `serve` and `"_schema": "run-manifest-v1"`, and nothing else is needed to run the app.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) with its name, version and licence, plus the STIX Two Text font and its licence.
Every shipped package and bundled font uses one of these licences: MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1.
The app uses only Postgres, MinIO and Mailpit as backing services. The shipped packages include no other database, cache, queue or embedded datastore, and no realtime or PDF web service.
The provided service configuration (the compose files and the dev environment values) is left unchanged.
All application source, server and client, is TypeScript, compiled by the `build` command, and `package-lock.json` is committed.
